author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Verify a CHD before replacing the original disc image
summary: Check the container and transfer without modifying the files. Keep the original disc dump until integrity checks and a gameplay test both succeed.
heroAlt: Original diagram showing a disc-image archive passing a checksum gate before entering a game library

blocks.text: Use your own disc dump and a current chdman from the official MAME distribution. Keep enough space for the original throughout verification. Perform these checks on a computer before transferring the CHD to Android. Identify whether the source is a DVD or a CD with track metadata. Keep the CUE file when it describes a BIN image.

Run `chdman info -i "Game.chd"` in the folder containing the archive. Record the media information, compression, hunk size and reported hashes. This checks whether the tool can read the container information. It does not verify all stored data. If the command fails, keep the error output and original dump for diagnosis.

Run `chdman verify -i "Game.chd"` and wait for successful completion. Do not add --fix or -f: that option modifies the input file. A delta CHD needs its matching parent CHD. A missing-parent error does not by itself prove that game data is corrupt. Keep the result together with the name of the file you checked.

After copying the CHD, compare a cryptographic hash of the computer file and destination file if your tools support this. Matching hashes confirm that the transfer preserved the same bytes. Then start the game normally, reach gameplay, load a known in-game save and test another loading screen. Container integrity alone cannot establish the quality of the original dump or emulator compatibility.
Return to the untouched source if checks fail

Keep the original until integrity and gameplay checks pass. If conversion fails verification, recreate the CHD from that original. Avoid repairing your only copy. Use the appropriate CD or DVD conversion workflow and retain track information for multi-track media. A small file or a successful startup logo does not replace a complete integrity check.
